evidence: PRESERVATION. Compared DRAFT.txt with SOURCE.txt word by word. The middle sentence is identical character for character ('The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc.'), as the_change says. Two parts changed, as the_change says. (1) 'especially if it relates to trauma and memory.' became 'especially if it has to do with trauma or memories.' 'relates to' and 'has to do with' are the same relation. 'and memory' to 'or memories' is the only shift worth noting: read as 'both', 'and' would be narrower than 'or', but in an 'especially if' clause 'trauma and memory' reads as two triggers, and 'especially' only emphasizes: the base claim 'Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal' is outside the draft and untouched. I find no added condition or claim. (2) 'So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!' became 'So take it as an image and get some outside help!' Same two imperatives, same reader, same exclamation, same strength. 'help outside of yourself' to 'outside help' keeps the sense (help from beyond oneself); in this section the help is people and support ('getting support', 'who would be a good person to help me'), so it is not narrowed to professionals. Nothing is added (no claim, condition, person or number) and nothing of his is dropped; the change does not say it restores anything. The meaning to keep (the imagery is symbolic, not proof of history; take it as image and look outside yourself) is intact. CONTEXT. The draft occurs once, as the section's closing REMEMBER paragraph. 'it' is the hypnotic imagery throughout, as in the approved paragraph. It reads in his voice (caps label parallel to 'NOTE:', exclamation, 'etc.'), and 'take it as an image' echoes the section's own 'symbolic form' ask. TELLS. Went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the paragraph as it would read: none PRESENT in the changed words. Rows I weighed and ruled out on the merits: T29 (the last sentence is a 'So...' line, but without it the paragraph has no instruction at all; 'get some outside help' is a new consideration, which T29 excludes, and the claim, mechanism, instruction shape is the approved paragraph's own); T28 (ADMISSION.json says this is not the end of its section, but CONTEXT.txt shows it is the section's last paragraph, so I judged T28 on that fact: it ends on a caution with a directive, not on healing, reassurance or a recap of what the reader learned); T02, T13, T09 (one short paragraph, not a run of compressed commands; the sentences carry unequal weight, a long uneven list ending 'fears etc.' next to a short command; the change adds no slot-filling sentence of its own); T21 (the packed sentence is the middle one, unchanged, see lint); T15 (the swaps go to plainer, more likely wording, and the structure is the source's by design); T25 and T19 ('REMEMBER:' is a label like 'NOTE:' earlier in the section, unchanged); C02 (same 'it' chain as the source). LINT. B4/E15 list or packed sentence: accepted. The flagged sentence is the middle one, unchanged from the paragraph he approved (batch 470) and not among the swapped sentences. It is an open list ('etc.') of how the mind transforms imagery, which is the sentence's content, and the section's other lists end the same way ('chemicals etc.', 'moral issues etc.', 'dissociation etc.'). D9 follows the source order: accepted. A sentence-level swap keeps the source's order by design and preservation requires that; I checked T13 and T09 above. O45 safety line ('So take it as an image and get some outside help!'): accepted. It is the paragraph's own closing caution, in the working copy he approved as 'So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!'; the change rewords it in place and adds or repeats no safety line, and dropping it would be a cut that needs his approval. It also does a job right here: what to do with the imagery that came, which is different from the section's advice on asking for capacity. I could not check the rest of the article for the same line (only this section is in my files).
